claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your child or children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son **Alex**.

Before I can assess eligibility, I need to gather some details about Alex and your circumstances. Let me start:

**How old is Alex, and does he currently live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 17 and yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is Alex in full-time education, such as school, college, or university?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask one more important question:

**Is Alex in work or receiving any benefits? If so, what is he doing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he works full-time at the local supermarket.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. I have one final question before I can make my assessment:

**What is Alex's nationality, and are you a UK resident?** (For example, are you both British citizens, or do you have settled status in the UK?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a UK resident - I live here in Manchester. We're both British citizens.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Let me now read the official Child Benefit eligibility rules to ensure I give you an accurate assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official Child Benefit eligibility rules, I can now provide you with my assessment.

Unfortunately, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you would normally still qualify for a child aged 16 or over if they stay in approved education or training. However, Alex is currently:
- 17 years old
- Working full-time (24 hours or more per week at the supermarket)
- Not in approved education or training

The rules specifically state: **"You'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training."**

Since Alex is in full-time paid work and is not in any approved education or training, he no longer qualifies for Child Benefit.

If Alex were to leave his job and re-enter education or training, you could potentially claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks while he searches for a new position with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, in his current circumstances, you would not be eligible.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I see, that's disappointing but I understand. Thank you for explaining that to me clearly. So basically once he started working full-time, that ended my eligibility. I appreciate your help!
